Ramen at Yamada's
Go with Mr. Tanaka to Mr. Yamada's ramen shop: buy a ticket at the machine, choose how firm your noodles are, get your own water, learn how to eat and what to say when you leave.
Meet Mr. Tanaka
Get to Yamada's
Buy a ticket at the ticket machine
Enjoy your ramen
Say thank you and leave
I'm getting hungry. Shall we go and eat ramen? I know a really good place.
Yes, I'd love to go.
Yes, I'll come.
I don't eat ramen.
Ah, I see. But they have udon too. Will you think about it?
Walking down Sakura Street, you reach a small shop. The red curtain says 「やまだ食堂」.
「食堂」 is a place to eat meals. This is Mr. Yamada's shop.
Welcome! Oh, Mr. Tanaka. Brought a friend today?
Nice to meet you. Thank you for having me.
Hello.
Haha, full of energy. But first, a proper greeting.
Here you buy a ticket at the ticket machine first. Here's the menu.
The machine's buttons: shoyu 800 yen, miso 900 yen, shio 800 yen, gyoza 400 yen, extra noodles (oomori) 100 yen.
Which ramen will you have? I'll have shoyu.
I'll have miso ramen.
I'll have shoyu ramen.
I'll have shio ramen.
I'll gladly have the ramen.
We haven't started eating yet. Say "~ ni shimasu" (I'll have ~). Which one will you have?
Will you have gyoza too? Gyoza is 400 yen. With the miso ramen, how much is that in total?
Could you say that once more, please?
Miso is 900 yen, gyoza is 400 yen. 900 plus 400 is 1,300 yen.
Will you have gyoza too? Gyoza is 400 yen. With the ramen, how much is that in total?
Could you say that once more, please?
Ramen is 800 yen, gyoza is 400 yen. 800 plus 400 is 1,200 yen.
You put the money in and press the buttons. Two tickets come out.
Okay, your tickets please. How firm would you like your noodles?
Regular, please.
Medium-firm, please.
Firm.
Haha, you should say "~ de onegaishimasu". Say it again!
Water is self-service. It's over there.
Thank you. I'll pour it.
Where is the water?
Excuse me, staff, water please.
Heh, it's over there. Next to the blue cup.
It's self-service here. Let's pour our own.
Here you go! It's hot, be careful.
I'll gladly have some.
Thank you. I'll gladly have some.
It's fine to slurp when you eat ramen. In Japan it means "delicious".
It's okay to make noise?
Making noise is not allowed.
No, with ramen it's fine. Give it a try.
Well, how does it taste?
It's delicious! The broth is so hot.
It's good.
It's okay.
Just okay?! Haha, how honest. Have a bit more.
If you want a little more noodles, there's kaedama (extra noodles). 100 yen.
I'm full. No thank you.
Yes, I'd like a little more.
Don't need it.
Great! Then buy one more 100-yen ticket.
Haha, straight to the point. All right then.
You finish your bowl of ramen. Your stomach is full, and so is your heart. You leave the shop.
Thank you very much! Come again.
Thank you for the meal. It was delicious.
Thanks.
I'll gladly have some.
Yes. If you say "gochisousama deshita" it makes me very happy.
Haha, you've already eaten! You should say "gochisousama deshita".
This is my favourite place. Come by any time from now on.

Summary: "~ ni shimasu" (I'll have ~), "~ de onegaishimasu" (~, please), "zenbu de, ikura desu ka" (how much altogether?). At a ramen shop: buy a ticket at the machine, water is self-service, and slurping is fine!
